business_model.claim: CoreCivic sells government-partner solutions: corrections and detention management, residential reentry centers, and government real estate. It describes itself as the nation's largest owner of partnership correctional, detention and residential reentry facilities.
quotes: we provide a broad range of solutions to government partners that serve the public good through corrections and detention management

business_model.claim: Customers are mainly federal, state and local government agencies. Federal agencies (ICE, the US Marshals Service and the Bureau of Prisons) were 54% of total revenue in 2025.
quotes: Our customers primarily consist of federal, state, and local government agencies.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 earnings release.
business_model.claim: The federal share of revenue stayed close to the 2025 level in the third quarter of 2026. Federal customers in the Residential segment were 53% of total revenue, against 55% a year earlier. Their revenue rose $71.3 million, or 22.2%, mainly on higher occupancy at ICE facilities and per diem increases.
quotes: The federal customers in our Residential segment generated 53% and 55% of our total revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 segment table.
business_model.claim: The 2025 10-K reported three segments: Safety, Community and Properties. Safety contributed 91.7% of 2025 segment net operating income, Community 5.1% and Properties 3.2%. Properties holds correctional real estate leased to government agencies.
quotes: CoreCivic Properties segment, consisting of five correctional real estate properties owned by CoreCivic held for lease to government agencies.

business_model.claim: The September 2026 10-Q describes a different segment structure: Residential, Services and Properties. Residential operated 64 correctional, detention and reentry facilities, 56 of them owned or controlled via long-term lease. Services provides mail order pharmacy services to over 600 correctional facilities, plus transportation and electronic monitoring.
quotes: Through our CoreCivic Services segment, we provided mail order pharmacy services to over 600 correctional facilities

business_model.basis: Stated in 10-K Item 1 and the Item 1A risk factors.
business_model.claim: In the facility-operating segments, pricing is a per diem rate for bed capacity and services. It is based on actual occupancy or a minimum guaranteed occupancy, so revenue moves with how many beds government customers use.
quotes: we are compensated for providing bed capacity and correctional, detention, and residential reentry services at a per diem rate based upon actual or minimum guaranteed occupancy levels

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K and the Q3 2026 release. The operating-leverage link comes from the fixed-cost statement and is inferred.
business_model.claim: Occupancy is a key driver. Average compensated occupancy rose to 77% in 2025 from 75% in 2024. Residential occupancy was 84.0% in the third quarter of 2026 against 76.7% a year earlier. A substantial portion of costs is fixed, so changes in occupancy have a large effect on profitability.
quotes: a substantial portion of our cost structure is fixed
Occupancy levels in our Residential segment increased to 84.0% in the third quarter of 2026 from 76.7% in the third quarter of 2025.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-Q and 10-K MD&A and risk factors.
business_model.claim: Federal immigration detention demand, mainly from ICE, is the main growth driver. The number of people cared for under ICE contracts is up approximately 8,100, or 80.1%, from the start of 2025 through September 30, 2026. The company ties demand to the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, which appropriates $75 billion to ICE.
quotes: The number of people we care for under contracts with ICE has increased by approximately 8,100 individuals, or 80.1%, from the beginning of 2025 through September 30, 2026.
OBBBA appropriates a total of $75 billion in mandatory funding to ICE for immigration enforcement activities and to increase detention capacity.

business_model.basis: Stated in the Q3 2026 release. The start-up cost point is from the 10-K risk factors.
business_model.claim: Activating idle facilities adds revenue. Four newly activated facilities are expected to generate about $320.0 million of annual revenue once fully activated and contributed $19.9 million of net operating income in the third quarter of 2026. Residential operating margin was relatively flat at 22.3% against 22.5% because the facilities are not yet at a fully activated margin.
quotes: These four facilities are expected to generate total annual revenue of approximately $320.0 million once fully activated.
During the three months ended September 30, 2026, these four facilities generated net operating income, or revenue less operating expenses, of $19.9 million.

business_model.claim: Revenue grew strongly. Third quarter 2026 revenue was 744,094 against 580,437 a year earlier, and nine-month revenue was 2,043,740 against 1,607,229 (table in thousands). Operating expenses were 586,922 in the third quarter, with general and administrative at 56,406 and depreciation and amortization at 33,917.
Labor is the largest cost. About 62% of operating expenses are salaries and benefits, and staff turnover and wage pressure are a cost driver.
quotes: Approximately 62% of our operating expenses consist of salaries and benefits.

business_model.claim: The Services segment grew through the April 1, 2026 acquisition of Clinical Solutions Pharmacy. Services net operating income rose $8.5 million to $9.6 million from $1.1 million a year earlier.
quotes: Net operating income in the CoreCivic Services segment increased $8.5 million, to $9.6 million in the third quarter of 2026 from $1.1 million in the prior year quarter.

business_model.basis: Stated in the release, the income statement and the 10-K risk factors. The reading that the gain is non-recurring is inferred from the company's special-items reconciliation.
business_model.claim: The company sold four detention facilities to the federal government (DHS) for $2.2 billion of gross proceeds. It expects to keep managing them under ICE management contracts, so it moves from owner-operator to operator for these sites. The sales produced a one-time gain of 1,770,664 (table in thousands). Net income of $1,344.1 million compares with Adjusted Net Income of $45.7 million.
quotes: We currently expect to continue to manage these four facilities under existing management contracts with ICE
Excluding these special items, Adjusted Net Income was $45.7 million, or $0.49 per diluted share

business_model.basis: Stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A.
business_model.claim: Contracts carry termination and renewal risk. Most facility contracts allow the agency to terminate at any time without cause. material_events.claim: CoreCivic sold four detention facilities with 7,187 beds to the U.S. government (DHS) for gross proceeds of $2.2 billion. The Q3 2026 income statement shows a gain on sale of real estate assets, net, of 1,770,664 (table in thousands).
quotes: Sold four detention facilities containing 7,187 beds for gross proceeds of $2.2 billion

material_events.claim: The company redeemed in full the remaining 4.75% 2027 senior notes ($238.5 million outstanding). It also paid off the Revolving Credit Facility and the term loans with facility sale proceeds.
quotes: Additionally, we redeemed in full the 4.75% senior unsecured notes issued in October 2017 with an original principal amount of $250.0 million (2027 Notes) that remained outstanding, which amounted to $238.5 million, on August 12, 2026 (Redemption Date).

material_events.basis: stated in the earnings release; the date is given in the capital strategy section of the same release
material_events.claim: CoreCivic entered into a $500 million accelerated share repurchase agreement. Final settlement is scheduled before the end of the second quarter of 2027.
quotes: Entered into $500 million Accelerated Share Repurchase Agreement (ASR)

material_events.claim: The board increased the share repurchase authorization, leaving $755.8 million available before any further ASR settlements.
quotes: Including the additional authorization, we have $755.8 million of repurchase authorization available under the share repurchase program, before any additional repurchase settlements occur under the ASR Agreement.

material_events.claim: CEO transition: Patrick D. Swindle stepped down as President and CEO for health reasons, and Lucibeth N. Mayberry was appointed President and CEO.
quotes: Patrick D. Swindle stepped down as President and Chief Executive Officer due to health reasons.

material_events.basis: the acquisition is stated in the release; the cash outflow is from the 10-Q cash flow statement, and linking the two is an inference
material_events.claim: CoreCivic acquired Clinical Solutions Pharmacy (CSP), a mail order pharmacy business in the CoreCivic Services segment. The nine-month cash flow statement shows acquisitions, net of cash acquired, of 142,783 (table in thousands).
quotes: the acquisition on April 1, 2026 of Clinical Solutions Pharmacy (CSP) in the CoreCivic Services segment

material_events.claim: ICE awarded CoreCivic a new five-year management contract to activate the previously idled Appleton Detention Facility. The contract commenced on August 11, 2026.
quotes: On August 3, 2026, we were awarded a new management contract with ICE to utilize the Appleton Facility.

risks.basis: Termination right and concentration are stated in the release. The consequence for revenue is inferred.
risks.claim: Federal customers in the Residential segment generated 53% of total revenue in the latest quarter. All ICE contracts, including those at the facilities sold to DHS, can be terminated for non-appropriation or convenience.
quotes: However, since all of our contracts with ICE provide it with the ability to terminate our contracts for non-appropriation of funds or for convenience, we can provide no assurance that we will continue to manage these facilities in the future, or that the terms of the management agreements will remain the same.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors. Renewal outcomes after the 10-K date are not in the evidence.
risks.claim: 35 facility contracts were scheduled to expire on or before the end of 2026. They earned $688.1 million, or 31% of total revenue, in the prior year, and 13 of them have no renewal options.
quotes: The aggregate revenue earned during the year ended December 31, 2025 for the 35 contracts with scheduled maturity dates, notwithstanding contractual renewal options, on or before December 31, 2026 was $688.1 million, or 31% of total revenue.

risks.basis: The risk is stated in the 10-K. The counter figures are in the Q3 release.
risks.claim: ICE is using non-traditional and government-owned detention capacity, which could divert occupancy from the company's facilities and undercut the growth case.
quotes: Utilization of additional forms of detention options, including through governmental ownership of detention facilities, could divert potential occupancy from our facilities, and thereby have an adverse impact on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factor and in the Q3 release. The effect on future margins is inferred, and no modified terms are in the evidence.
risks.claim: Sales of owned facilities to DHS for $2.2 billion gross proceeds convert owned assets into management-only positions. The guidance is based on an estimate because the management contracts have not been modified.
quotes: Even if we were to be engaged by a governmental customer to operate the facility following the sale, our operation of the facility pursuant to a management agreement may be less profitable than our ownership of the facility, and there can be no assurance that such governmental customer will not terminate the management contract associated with such facility or engage another operator to manage such facility.

Although we and ICE have not yet modified the management contracts for these facilities to reflect the change in ownership, the range of our guidance incorporates our best estimate of the financial impact of the change in ownership.

risks.basis: The policy risk is stated in the 10-K. The funding counter is stated in the 10-K and 10-Q MD&A.
risks.claim: Demand depends on federal policy and administration priorities. The 10-K notes that future administrations could restrict federal use of private detention.
quotes: It is possible future administrations could issue executive orders restricting the use of private correctional and detention facilities by the federal government.

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K, filed February 2026. The bill's current status and its application to facilities now owned by DHS are not in the evidence.
risks.claim: Proposed California legislation (AB1633) would impose a 50% tax on gross receipts of private detention facility operators, if enacted.
quotes: Furthermore, recently proposed legislation in California, Assembly Bill 1633, or AB1633, would impose an annual tax equal to 50% of the gross receipts of private detention facility operators beginning on January 1, 2027, if enacted into law.

risks.basis: Balances and statement lines are stated in F1 and F3. The link between the operating outflow and taxes is inferred.
risks.claim: Accounts receivable, net, rose to 535,336 from 446,224 (table in thousands). Nine-month operating cash flow was (266,625) (table in thousands), and federal customers are generally not paid until the government reopens after a shutdown. The evidence suggests this risk is currently mitigated.
quotes: While we have historically been required to continue to perform under our government contracts during government shutdowns, we are generally not paid until the government reopens.

risks.basis: Stated in the Q3 release and the 10-Q MD&A. Current litigation status is not in the evidence.
risks.claim: Results depend on the pace of activating facilities. The facilities under activation generated $19.9 million of net operating income in the quarter, have not reached a fully activated margin, and are expected to generate approximately $320.0 million of annual revenue once fully activated. Intake at one was delayed by a permit lawsuit.
quotes: Because these four facilities continue to be in various stages of activation, they are not yet contributing at a fully activated margin percentage.
The City of Leavenworth filed a lawsuit alleging that a Special Use Permit, or SUP, was required to activate the facility, which resulted in a delay in the intake process.

risks.basis: Stated in a secondary press report. Its current relevance is inferred and is low confidence.
risks.claim: A press report states that the U.S. Department of Justice opened a civil rights investigation into CoreCivic and its Trousdale Turner facility in 2024. No outcome appears in the evidence.
quotes: The U.S. Department of Justice has opened an investigation into private prison company CoreCivic and Trousdale Turner Correctional Center, which it manages, over alleged civil rights violations.
